text: For a few weeks, Mars is moving through your 1st house, and its energy lands on you directly. This is the personal stretch of its roughly two-year loop around your chart, the point where the planet of drive crosses the part of the sky that means you: your body, your presence, the face you show first. You feel it as fuel. Projects you have been circling suddenly look startable. You speak up faster, walk faster, and care less about who is watching. People notice you more during this pass because there is simply more of you in the room. The gift of the period is initiative. Whatever you begin now carries extra push, so it is a natural season for the first move: the application, the opening conversation, the training plan, the thing you keep saying you will start. Your body wants work while Mars is here, and hard physical effort tends to steady the mood in a way rest does not. The cost of the period is friction. The same current that gets you moving shortens your fuse. Small obstacles, slow lines, slow drivers, slow colleagues, can feel like personal insults. Haste is the classic trouble: rushing, bumping into things, saying the sharp sentence before the second thought arrives. Not every irritation this month is worth the charge you have available for it. If Mars happens to be in its retrograde stretch, it can linger here for months instead of weeks, and the push turns inward: the same drive, with more stalls and second passes, asking you to redo a start rather than force it. Either way the shape of the season is the same. It begins with restlessness, peaks in a stretch where you feel almost too awake, and settles as Mars crosses into the next house and the heat moves off you. Used well, this pass sets the tone for the next two years of effort, because what you launch or claim now is what the rest of the cycle builds on. So aim it. Pick the one or two fronts that deserve the surge, spend the temper in exercise instead of arguments where you can, and let yourself be a little louder than usual on your own behalf. Wanting things openly is not a flaw this month. It is the weather.

Money gets loud while Mars moves through your 2nd house. For a few weeks, the planet of drive works the part of your chart that handles income, spending, and the things you own, and everything in that zone speeds up. You may feel a real push to earn: extra shifts appeal, side income looks worth the trouble, and the gap between what you have and what you want turns from a fact into an itch. Effort put toward money tends to pay in this window, because you have the stamina for it and the appetite. The same heat runs the other direction too. Spending gets impulsive here, particularly on gear, tools, and anything that promises capability. The purchase feels decisive in the moment and optional a week later. It helps to know the tilt is temporary: this is a season of wanting, not a change in your character. Possessions carry an extra charge under this pass. A borrowed thing returned late, a roommate using your stuff, a vendor rounding up: small property frictions can spark anger out of scale with the object, because right now what is yours stands for your ground. Values get the same defense. You argue harder than usual about what is fair, what something costs, and what your work is worth, and a budgeting conversation at home can heat up fast. Naming the real subject early, respect, security, credit, keeps the small fight small. Should Mars station retrograde during this pass, the money theme stretches from weeks into months, often with a redo built in: a renegotiation, a returned purchase, a second look at what an arrangement actually pays. Otherwise the arc is quick. The wanting builds, peaks in a stretch where every price tag seems to demand a decision, and eases as Mars moves on. What the period is for, underneath, is a live audit of worth. It shows you where your earning is underpowered, where your spending is a mood, and which of your possessions actually function as ground. Push on the first, watch the second, and thank the third. A few weeks of honest hustle here can leave your accounts, and your sense of what you are worth, in noticeably better shape than the quiet months before it.

While Mars crosses your 3rd house, your words pick up speed. This is the part of your chart that runs daily communication, short trips, siblings and neighbors, the whole traffic of ordinary information, and for a few weeks Mars turns the volume up on all of it. Your mind is quicker than usual and more combative. You see the flaw in an argument immediately, the reply arrives before the other person finishes, and you have little patience for meetings that circle. Used deliberately, this is a fine window for anything that needs verbal push: the hard email you keep postponing, the pitch, the negotiation over details, the letter that needs one intense week. You can say difficult things cleanly right now, and plain speech from you lands with force. The risk is that everything starts to sound like a debate. Sharp words come easily under this pass, and the people closest to the crossfire are often the everyday ones: a sibling, a neighbor, the group chat, the coworker one desk over. A remark you experience as efficient can land as cutting, and small misunderstandings escalate fast because nobody feels like conceding. Reading a message twice before sending it saves real cleanup later. The pace of daily life rises with the pace of talk. Errands multiply, the calendar fills with short runs, and impatience follows you into traffic, where haste costs the most. Rushing through the routine layer of life is the signature trouble of this transit; slowing down a notch covers most of it. In a round where Mars turns retrograde here, the visit runs long, and old conversations circle back: an argument reopens, a message needs a second answer, a decision made quickly asks to be restated with care. The general arc runs hot to warm. Early on, the mind races and the tongue leads. At the peak, everything feels debatable. Then Mars moves along, the pace drops, and you can hear how much you got said. What this season is for is traction in the small stuff: calls made, letters sent, questions finally asked, positions finally stated. If you point the sharpness at problems instead of people, you come out the other side with a cleared backlog and a few overdue truths on the record, and the neighborhood is still speaking to you.

Mars is moving through your 4th house, and the heat has gone home. For a few weeks, the drive that usually pours into the outside world runs through your private base: the household, the family, the walls themselves, and the older layers of feeling underneath them. On the practical surface, this is a season of domestic energy. Repairs get done, rooms get cleared, moves and renovations that have idled suddenly find muscle. Physical work on your own place is one of the most satisfying uses of this pass, and often the calmest. Under the surface, the pressure is emotional. Mars here has a way of warming up old anger: friction with parents, a relative's remark that lands on a decades-old bruise, a household pattern you have tolerated for years suddenly feeling intolerable. Arguments during this stretch tend to happen in kitchens and hallways rather than offices, and they are rarely about the dish or the thermostat they start with. When a small dispute flares at home, it usually points to a real negotiation that has been postponed: about space, labor, money, or say. Having that negotiation on purpose beats having it sideways. People who share your roof feel the weather too, so some of the flare-ups will not start with you; the season asks for a longer fuse precisely where your fuse is shortest. A retrograde station in this house can hold the domestic season open for months, often circling an unresolved family matter or a project that needs a second attempt before it holds. The arc of the pass usually moves from restlessness to eruption to repair: early on the house just feels tight, mid-transit something says itself out loud, and by the end there is a chance to rebuild on more honest ground. That is the real work of the period. Your base is where your energy comes from, and this transit shows you exactly where the base leaks: which room, which relationship, which old resentment. Effort spent there now is not a detour from your ambitions but the maintenance under them. When Mars moves on, the ideal souvenir is a home that is a little more yours: a fixed thing, a said thing, and a bit more room to breathe in the place you return to every night.

Wanting comes back first. As Mars moves through your 5th house, the part of your chart that runs romance, play, creative work, and children heats up, and for a few weeks you remember what it is to want something just because it lights you up. Desire is direct under this pass. If you are drawn to someone, you feel like doing something about it: the message gets sent, the invitation gets made, the interest stops hiding. Romance begun or rekindled now tends to burn hot and move fast, which is its charm and its caution in one. In an existing relationship, the same current can turn into more pursuit and more sparks, and also into quicker quarrels over attention and pride; the couple that plays together spends this transit better than the couple that only manages logistics. Creative work gets the same fuel. Projects you love pull at you, and this is a strong window for making things with force in them: bold drafts, loud rehearsals, the version of the piece you were too careful to try before. The inner critic is quieter than the appetite right now, and output beats polish. Play sharpens into competition here. Games matter more than they should, sports get intense, and you may catch yourself needing to win the board game. Children in your life, your own or others', may run hotter too: more energy, more defiance, more need for something physical to do with the charge. Appetite for risk rises across the board, in games, in flirtation, in stakes generally, and the thrill is real; the size of the bet is the thing to keep an eye on while the mood is this bold. Some rounds, Mars turns retrograde mid-pass and the season runs long; an old flame, an old project, or an old rivalry may circle back for a second look. Most passes are quicker: the spark, a peak where you feel ten years younger, then the slow cooling as Mars moves on. Take the season at its word while it lasts. Make the thing, ask the person, play the game hard. The point of this stretch is not what it produces, though it often produces plenty. It is the reminder that your fire is not only for work, and that joy responds to pursuit just like everything else.

The pace of your working days rises while Mars moves through your 6th house. This is the zone of routine, tasks, service, and the daily upkeep of the body, and Mars in it for a few weeks turns ordinary workload into a campaign. You want the backlog gone. Lists get attacked, inboxes get cleared, and the sheer output you can produce in this window surprises people, sometimes including you. It is one of the best stretches in Mars's two-year round for grinding through what you have been avoiding: the filing, the fixes, the appointments, the tedious middle of every project. The friction shows up where the work is shared. Colleagues who move slower than you, processes that add steps, a boss who reprioritizes your day: all of it grates more than usual, and workplace quarrels under this transit are common and usually about method rather than substance. You think there is a right way to do the task and you can see it. The season's discipline is remembering that being correct and being abrasive can arrive in the same sentence if you are not careful. The body is the other front. Mars here gives real physical energy and asks for an outlet, so training goes well now, and hard routine effort, running, lifting, long walks, burns off the irritation that would otherwise land on coworkers. Pushed too far, the same drive becomes the classic overwork pattern: skipped meals, short sleep, small injuries from hurrying, the run-down week that follows a month of running hot. Fatigue during this pass is information, not weakness. A station and retrograde here turn the pass into months rather than weeks, and the theme becomes rework: redoing a process, revisiting a health habit, fixing the fix. The usual arc is more brisk, a ramp of momentum, a peak of near-compulsive productivity, then an easing as the planet moves on and the to-do list stops shouting. What the season offers, taken well, is repair of the machinery of your life. Routines that were slack get tightened, work that was drifting gets finished, and the body gets reminded it is built for effort. If you spend the heat on tasks and training rather than on the people beside you, you come out lean, caught up, and noticeably harder to rattle.

For a few weeks the heat is not in you, it is across the table. Mars moving through your 7th house charges the zone of partnership: spouses, business partners, close collaborators, and open opponents. The classic experience of this pass is that other people seem to have gotten pushier. Your partner has demands. The client wants to renegotiate. Someone contests a decision you thought was settled. It can feel like the world picked a fight, but the mechanics are more even than that: this transit heats the space between you and others, and both ends of every relationship feel it. Conflict that surfaces now is rarely new. Mars tends to expose the disagreement that was already there, the imbalance of labor, the unspoken resentment, the term of the deal that one side quietly stopped honoring. That makes this an uncomfortable season and a genuinely useful one, because issues you can see can be negotiated, and issues kept polite cannot. Couples often do their overdue arguing during this stretch and come out cleaner, provided the fight stays about the issue instead of becoming a contest of who wins. Fighting fair is the whole art of the transit: direct about the complaint, specific about the ask, done without the extra sentence that turns a negotiation into a wound. The pass also energizes partnership in the plain sense. Working closely with one other person, a co-founder, a doubles partner, a co-author, gains drive now, and a well-matched partner can push you further in these weeks than you would push alone. Rivals count here too: a competitor who names your weak point is doing you a rough favor. A retrograde here can stretch the negotiating season across several months, with old disputes reopening for a final settlement rather than a rematch. Most passes run shorter: tension builds, something gets said, terms get redrawn, and the temperature drops as Mars moves on. What remains afterward is the point. Relationships that survive an honest quarrel tend to hold better than ones preserved by silence, and this transit is the scheduled honesty. Meet the pushback instead of dodging it, keep your side of the fight clean, and the people worth keeping will still be there when the weather passes, standing on clearer terms.

Mars is crossing your 8th house, the part of your chart that handles shared resources, debts, intimacy, and power, and for a few weeks the charged material of life gets more charged. On the money side, the themes are joint: the account you share, the loan, the tax question, the inheritance, the split. Disputes over who owes what and who controls what are the classic surface of this transit, and they arrive with more temper than bookkeeping usually deserves, because under this house money stands for trust. A billing fight with an institution, a settlement that needs pushing, a partner whose spending suddenly bothers you: whatever form it takes, the season rewards facing the tangle directly and reading the fine print while your nerve is up. Intimacy is the other current. Desire runs deeper and more intense under this pass, less playful than possessive, and closeness can swing between magnetic and combative in the same week. Power is the real subject: who reaches, who withholds, who decides. If a struggle for control has been running quietly in a close bond, Mars here tends to bring it into the open, which is turbulent and, handled honestly, clarifying. The same intensity turns inward too. This transit has a way of surfacing your own buried heat, the resentment you never voiced, the fear under a habit, the motive you would rather not have. Meeting that material takes more courage than any argument, and the weeks of this pass supply exactly that kind of nerve. When a retrograde holds Mars in this house, the season runs long, often circling one financial entanglement or one relational knot until it is actually undone rather than re-buried. The ordinary arc is shorter and steep: pressure builds, something private comes to a head, and the release when it resolves is real. Treat the period as a controlled burn. Settle the debt conversation you have been dreading, say the true thing inside the close relationship, look at the motive you have been stepping around. The 8th house is where things change by being faced, and Mars is the part of you willing to face them. What burns off in these weeks is mostly what you no longer needed, and what survives the heat, in your bonds and in yourself, you can finally trust.

Your convictions get muscle while Mars moves through your 9th house. This is the zone of beliefs, higher learning, long journeys, law, and the big picture, and for a few weeks you do not merely hold opinions, you champion them. Ideas feel worth fighting for now. You argue politics, religion, ethics, and strategy with more fire than usual, and you are drawn to people and books that think in large terms. At its best this is a crusading season in the good sense: real energy for the cause, the degree, the case, the message, and the stamina to push a big idea uphill. Teaching, publishing, and persuading all gain force under this pass, because you speak from conviction and it shows. The shadow is righteousness. Mars here can turn a viewpoint into a barricade, and debates into contests where being right matters more than being useful. The tell is contempt: the moment an opponent starts to look stupid rather than mistaken, the transit is driving. The strongest use of the season is aiming the fight at your own ignorance instead, attacking a subject you want to master, a qualification, a language, a hard book, with the aggression you might otherwise spend on strangers who vote wrong. Distance also pulls. Travel appeals under this transit, especially travel with effort in it, and a trip taken now tends toward the strenuous and memorable rather than the restful. Formal matters can heat up too, a filing, an appeal, a dispute over rules, and these reward prompt energetic handling rather than delay. On the rounds when Mars retrogrades here, the stay stretches out, and the revisiting is usually of belief itself: a position you defended loudly asks to be rechecked, a plan built on principle needs its premises tested. Most passes run quicker, from a swell of certainty, through a peak of argument and motion, to a settling where you can tell which convictions survived being used. That sorting is the gift. A few weeks of fighting for what you believe shows you, faster than years of quiet agreement, which beliefs are actually yours and which were furniture. Keep the fire and lose the sneer, and you come out of this season with a worldview that has been road-tested, and the energy to act on it.

Ambition wakes up hard when Mars enters your 10th house. For a few weeks the planet of drive occupies the most visible zone of your chart, the one that governs career, reputation, and standing, and the push you feel is upward. Work you have done quietly wants recognition now. Goals that seemed comfortably long-term suddenly feel urgent, and you have the energy to match: extra hours come easier, competitive instincts sharpen, and you find yourself volunteering for exactly the assignments you used to watch others take. This is one of the strongest windows in Mars's two-year circuit for a professional offensive: asking for the promotion, launching the venture, taking the visible role, going after the client everyone assumes is out of reach. Effort made in public tends to compound during this pass, because people are watching and what they see is force. The friction runs along the chain of command. Mars here has a well-earned reputation for clashes with authority: the boss whose caution reads as obstruction, the rule that feels personal, the board that wants one more review. Some of that resistance deserves the fight, and some is simply the cost of institutions; telling the two apart is the judgment call of the season. An open challenge to the wrong person at the wrong moment can undo months of standing, while the same energy channeled into visible results usually gets what the confrontation wanted anyway. Reputation is exposed both ways under this transit: wins are seen, and so are tantrums. Now and then a retrograde extends this career season by months, often with a strategy that must be revised mid-push or an ambition that needs redefining before it can land. The typical arc is cleaner: a climb of intensity, a peak where the stakes feel public and personal at once, then an easing as the planet moves on and the results start speaking for you. What the season builds, used well, is proof. Not the private kind, the kind on the record: the shipped thing, the closed deal, the title, the visible standard you set. Aim the surge at one or two objectives that genuinely matter, stay civil with the gatekeepers you still need, and let the work be the argument. A few weeks of directed ambition here can move your position more than a quiet year.

While Mars moves through your 11th house, your energy turns toward the group. This is the zone of friends, allies, teams, causes, and the longer-range hopes you steer by, and for a few weeks all of it gets an injection of drive. Collective effort appeals now. You want to organize the trip, rally the committee, push the project the group has talked about for a year, and your presence on any team becomes noticeably more forceful. A cause can catch fire in you during this pass: something you believed in mildly becomes something you will actually work for, and the willingness to do the unglamorous labor, the calls, the setup, the showing up, is the transit's best gift. Friendship gets the same intensity, in both directions. Plans with friends multiply and get more active, and old friends may pull you into their battles. But Mars in a group is Mars in close quarters, and friction inside teams is the season's classic trouble. Disagreements over direction turn personal, one member's pace irritates another, and you may find yourself the pushy one, certain the group would move if everyone just committed. Sometimes you are right, and the group needs the shove. Sometimes the shove costs an ally, and allies are the currency of this house. The working rule of the season: fight for the goal, not against the members. Quarrels among friends under this transit tend to be recoverable when the shared aim stays in view, and corrosive when they become tests of loyalty. Your own long-range goals deserve the same energy. This is a good stretch for taking a hope you have carried vaguely, the someday plan, and giving it a first concrete step and a deadline, ideally with someone else involved, since solitary resolutions have less traction here than shared ones. In a retrograde round the pass runs far longer, and an old alliance or an abandoned team project may circle back to be either revived or finally closed. The usual arc is shorter: enthusiasm gathers, the group hits its stormy patch, and things settle with the roster slightly changed and the mission clearer. That clarity is the point. When Mars moves on, you know which people pull with you, which cause is worth your labor, and which hope has become a plan.

Mars is moving through your 12th house, and the fire goes quiet without going out. This is the most hidden zone of your chart, the place of retreat, endings, and everything that runs beneath awareness, and Mars spends a few weeks here at the close of its roughly two-year circuit before it crosses into your 1st house and starts a new one. The felt experience is often frustration with no clear address. Your usual push seems to land on fog: efforts stall for invisible reasons, direct approaches misfire, and your energy runs lower than the calendar can explain. This is not failure; it is the wrong season for the frontal assault. Drive works indirectly now. Behind-the-scenes effort goes surprisingly well, the groundwork nobody sees, the research, the quiet preparation of a move you will make openly later, and helping someone with no audience carries a satisfaction that public wins briefly lose. Anger is the material to watch. Mars in this house tends to submerge irritation rather than express it, and buried anger has habits: the sudden snap at the wrong target, the accident born of distraction, the low mood that is actually fury with the label torn off. Simply asking yourself what you are angry about, and answering honestly, defuses more of this transit than willpower does. Old matters surface for settlement too, an unfinished conflict, a guilt, a pattern of quietly working against your own stated aims. Seen clearly, these are the last debts of the ending cycle asking to be paid before the new one opens. If Mars stations retrograde here, the underground season can run for months, and the digging goes deeper; rest becomes less a preference than a requirement. The arc of an ordinary pass moves from muffled restlessness, through a middle where you may feel oddly sidelined in your own life, to a genuine turn: energy returning as the planet approaches your 1st house. Treat the weeks accordingly. Reduce the frontal battles, tend the body with sleep and gentle effort, finish and file what is finishable, and let the plans ripen in the drawer. Seasons like this are how a two-year cycle empties itself out. What you release now you will not be carrying when the fire comes back, and it comes back soon.
